onboarding.title: Four steps to your first job

register.title: Sign up
register.body: Call the recruitment hotline and tell us your main skill and the province where you want to work.

verify.body: Create an account in the technician app and verify your identity with a valid ID document.

training.body: Learn how to accept jobs, confirm appointments with customers, install, and sign off with photos in the app.

jobs.title: Take jobs
jobs.body: Accept jobs near you, call the customer to confirm the appointment, then install and sign off together.

standards.title: Bluebolt technician standards
standards.lead: These four groups apply to lead technicians. Assistants and trainees need basic knowledge and a willingness to learn.

qualification.title: Qualifications and documents
qualification.i1: A vocational diploma or trade certificate in electronics and refrigeration, electrical engineering or mechatronics.
qualification.i2: Lead technicians have hands-on installation experience.
qualification.i3: A work safety certificate is a plus, especially for electrical safety and working at height.
qualification.i4: Documents to bring: a valid ID card, a trade certificate or proof of experience, and a criminal record certificate.

skills.title: Technical skills
skills.i1: Air conditioners: reading wiring diagrams, brazing copper pipe, charging refrigerant, pressure testing, evacuating the lines and positioning indoor and outdoor units correctly.
skills.i2: Fridges and washing machines: levelling, connecting water supply and drainage, and earthing to prevent electric shock.
skills.i3: TVs: drilling, fitting fixed, tilting or swivel brackets, then setting up and connecting to the internet.
skills.i4: Using a multimeter, a wall scanner and the phone app to receive jobs and send on-site photos.

conduct.title: Service conduct
conduct.i3: Polite communication, advice on the best mounting spot and a quick walkthrough of the appliance after installation.
conduct.i4: Cleaning up the work area before handover.

safety.title: Safety and compliance
safety.i1: Full protective gear: helmet, safety shoes and a harness when working at height.
safety.i2: Checking for current leakage with a voltage tester before touching any appliance.
safety.i3: Using materials of the right specification for copper pipe thickness and cable size.
safety.i4: Protecting the customer's home: covering surfaces when drilling or cutting, and not damaging walls, floors or furniture.

howToRegister.q: How do I sign up as a technician partner?
howToRegister.a: Call {phone} and say you want to join as a technician partner. Have your full name, mobile number, main working province and main skill ready, and the recruitment team will guide you through the next steps.

noCertificate.q: Can I sign up without a trade certificate?
noCertificate.a: You can still apply as an assistant or trainee if you have basic knowledge. The recruitment team will discuss the right role with you when they call back.

chooseArea.q: Can I choose where I work?
chooseArea.a: Yes. You choose your working province when you sign up, and jobs are suggested based on your area, skills and availability.

materials.q: Who does the customer pay for materials?

hours.q: What are the on-site working hours?

existing.q: I'm already a partner. Who do I call about a job in progress?
existing.a: Call {phone}, say you are a technician partner and give the job code so we can connect you with the right person.
